title: Station PRD v1
description: The MINT step of the station cell, as a document: one station's ex-ante work order, derived from its CONTRACT crossed with the CANDIDATE SUBSTRATE named by a consist manifest. It says what must be proven HERE to earn departure, and it is written BEFORE anything is exercised - a PRD assembled after the fills is a transcript, and a transcript cannot refuse. Rows key on the contract's value ids and on nothing else: per-train row ids (A1, F3) were the measured failure mode, because the same claim carried a different name on every train and therefore could not be verified downstream. A row whose value_id is not in the contract is a `proposed_value` and belongs in that array, where its only path into `rows` is a pull request against the contract.

station.description: Which cell in the line is minting this (e.g. `station-3-staging`). One PRD per station per candidate; a station that mints twice for one candidate has re-cut, and the second PRD cites the new manifest_sha256.

contract_id.description: The contract this station is bound by (e.g. `vexa-internal-staging-2026-09`). The law half of the derivation.

contract_sha256.description: sha256 of the contract file's bytes. The contract's identity IS its hash and rides in every verdict rendered under it, which is why a contract moves only by pull request - an edit invalidates the lineage on purpose and visibly.

manifest_sha256.description: sha256 of the consist manifest this PRD was derived against. The substrate half. A PRD and a station verdict that cite different manifests are describing different candidates, and that is a refusal, not a discrepancy.

candidate_sha.description: Carried redundantly with the manifest so a reader can check the two agree without fetching the manifest. They must.

rows.description: The work order. One row per contract value this station must exercise on THIS candidate. Empty is legal only for a station whose contract has no required_values, which no contract in this line has.

value_id.description: The contract's `required_values[].id`. The ONLY key. Matched by exact string downstream, so a typo is a missing proof rather than a silent pass.

claim.description: The contract's claim, quoted. Copied so the PRD is readable standalone; a copy that diverges from the contract is a finding the contract wins.

spec.description: The MINIMAL exercise that proves this claim against this candidate - the derivation, calibrated to the obligation and not to the rig. This is the part the substrate contributes: the same value id gets a different spec on a candidate that touches the join module than on one that does not.

slot.description: Where the proof will come from. `fills` - this station exercises it. `inherited` - an upstream station already proved it and this station verifies the signed claim rather than re-proving it (the whole reason the chain is cheaper than N full validations). `waiver` - a named human will accept it unproven; the name lands in values_proven.waived_by, never here.

inherited_from.description: The upstream station whose signed station-verdict carries this value. Required in spirit on every `inherited` row: an inheritance with no named source cannot be verified.

car.description: The manifest car this row exists because of, when the row is cargo-driven rather than a standing property of the environment. `<owner>/<repo>#<number>`.

proposed_values.description: Claims this candidate makes that NO contract value covers. Mandatory as an array (write `[]` when there are none) because the alternative is what this whole design refuses: a station inventing a row for one train, proving it, and having it evaporate at departure because no contract names it. A proposed value is a pull request against the contract, and until that PR merges the row is not a gate.

value_id.description: The id the value would carry if the contract accepted it. Reserved here so the PR and the PRD talk about the same thing.

rationale.description: Why the contract should carry this standing, beyond this train. A rationale that only argues for this candidate is an argument for a fill, not for a contract row.

pr.description: The contract pull request, once opened. Its absence means the value is still a proposal.

derived_at.description: When the derivation ran. Ex-ante means this instant precedes every `ts` in the fills log, and that ordering is checkable.

notes.description: Holes this PRD carries forward from the previous train rather than silently dropping.
